newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal minister sees jobs created in services.
newsitem.headline: Portugal minister sees jobs created in services.

text.p: Employment Minister Maria Joao Rodrigues said she expected jobs to be created in services, car, electronics and paper industries and to be lost in textiles, clothing, food and fisheries in Portugal in the coming years.
Asked to outline where jobs would be created and lost, she told Reuters on Friday night: "Jobs in Portugal will be created in services, for example, in health, education and culture."

She added: Other sectors that are creating jobs are linked to the automotive sector, electronics, paper and the derivatives of paper, and traditional industries, such as shoes, which are modernising."
"But at the same time we foresee that other industrial sectors are losing jobs, as in the case of textiles, clothing, and some food industries," the minister said.
"These sectors are modernising quickly in order to survive and in some cases cut back jobs," she added.
Rodrigues also said that jobs were being lost in fisheries.
She said jobs in agriculture were being created in rural tourism and projects to protect the environment.
"The government is interested in stimulating job creation in rural areas to prevent desertification," she said.
The minister said the government aimed to boost job creation by pursuing sound macroeconomic policies that reduced inflation and interest rates to stimulate conditions for investment.
"These macroeconomic policies are giving good results because we are obtaining reductions in real interest rates," she said.

The government also offered incentive programmes to industry to encourage businesses to recruit and train well-qualified people as well as programmes to encourage people to set up companies, she said.
